about: Place names the player is told (ink UI round, gen/ui/STYLE.md 'Place notifications'). region: the large banner shown when you walk into this section's region (sections sharing a region id show it once). landmarks: a vertical name plaque stands over the map entity id as you approach (江南百景圖's plaques), and a toast with the line from the painting's reading when you come within r metres of its footprint (or its point); top: the plaque's height when the map has none. Every name and line in 繁體, from the painting and its readings; src says where. Lore (round 2, gen/ui/r2_lore.md): long is the longer description under the toast's fold and in the 圖志 journal; quote and quoteSrc an exact line from a period or scholarly source; cite the sources as the player reads them; longSrc one note per claim (never shown); crop the map IDs that frame the painting's crop (tools/place_crops.mjs). Bundled for the page by tools/ui_data.mjs into web/public/assets/ui/places.json (short) and lore.json (long, fetched when needed). Every displayed field has an English sibling `<field>_en`, shown as a gloss under the Chinese when the viewer picks 中英 (Chinese stays the default).

region.name: 城門
region.src: map/sections.json S5 '城门'; 故宫 catalogue text (杨新): the gate tower is 东角子门, '位于汴京内城东南' (identification disputed)
region.long: 過了護城河上的平橋，便是全卷最高大的建築：城樓。這是哪一座城門，說法不一：故宮從東角子門之說；徐邦達、張安治據金人張公藥的跋詩「水門東去接隋渠」讀作東水門；余輝則說門額上只寫一個「門」字，畫的是「實情而非實景」。這裏用故宮之說。余輝又指出，這座城門沒有甕城，也不見垛口；一隊駱駝正從門洞走出城去，牽頭的像是胡人，進門頭一家便是稅務。
region.long_en: Across the flat bridge over the moat stands the tallest building in the whole scroll: the gate tower. Which gate it is, no one agrees: the Palace Museum follows the Dongjiaozi Gate reading; Xu Bangda and Zhang Anzhi, citing the line “The water gate eastward meets the Sui canal” in the colophon poem by the Jin writer Zhang Gongyao, read it as the East Water Gate; Yu Hui says the plaque bears only the single character “Gate,” and that the painter shows “the true situation, not the real view.” Here we use the Palace Museum's reading. Yu Hui also points out that this gate has no barbican and no crenellations; a string of camels is walking out of the gateway and out of the city, led by what looks like a man from the Western lands, and the first shop inside the gate is the Tax Office.
region.quote: 城門前後、城樓上下竟然沒有一兵一卒把守。
region.quote_en: Before and behind the gate, above and below the gate tower, there is not a single soldier standing guard.
region.quoteSrc: 余輝〈清明上河圖十大看點〉
region.cite: 故宮・徐邦達・張安治・余輝〈十大看點〉〈最後三問〉
region.cite_en: Palace Museum · Xu Bangda · Zhang Anzhi · Yu Hui, Ten Highlights and The Last Three Questions
longSrc: MHJ 33: 整幅画卷中，城门楼是一座最大的建筑物
SEC §3 Which gate: 东角子门 (the museum); 东水门 (徐邦达, 张安治, after the Jin colophon 水门东去接隋渠); composite (余辉)
COL: 张公药跋 水门东去接隋渠
YH21: 牌匾…就写了一个"门"字; YH15 看点十 (end) and 实情而非实景 (YH15 text)
YH15 看点七: 城门不是瓮城…连射箭的城垛也没有; 胡人模样的驭手; YH15 看点八: 城门内头一家是税务所
quote: YH15 看点七

landmarks.name: 稅務
landmarks.line: 貨到稅訖，車夫在此納稅。
landmarks.line_en: Goods arrive, tax is paid; the carters settle up here.
landmarks.src: 名画记 35 税务所; 余辉 2014 vignette 货到税讫; map: tax office (税务所 / 场务)
landmarks.long: 進了城門，街北緊貼城牆的頭一家，是一座敞開的廳屋，西間掛著一桿大秤，中間官員坐在長案後正要落筆。故宮名畫記說「有的研究者認為這是稅務所」：案上的紙卷或是「引子」，即商貨的通行憑證，沒有引子，稅就收得格外重。門外貨包堆著，貨主指著貨物和稅吏爭論，連城樓上的人也探頭張望。余輝更讀出一層意思：城門內頭一家本該是城防機關，如今卻改成了收稅的地方。
landmarks.long_en: Inside the gate, the first building on the north side of the street, hard against the city wall, is an open hall; a big steelyard hangs in the west bay, and in the middle an official sits behind a long desk about to put brush to paper. The Palace Museum's notes say “some researchers think this is a tax office”: the paper rolls on the desk may be the “yinzi,” a pass for merchants' goods, and without one the tax is charged especially heavy. Outside, bundles of goods are piled up, a merchant points at his goods and argues with the tax clerk, and even the people up on the gate tower lean out to look. Yu Hui reads one more layer into it: the first building inside a city gate ought to be a defence office, and here it has been turned into a place that collects tax.
landmarks.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝〈十大看點〉〈最後三問〉・畫中所見
landmarks.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui, Ten Highlights and The Last Three Questions · What the painting shows
longSrc: map S5.bld.tax_office: open hall, frame scale in the west bay, official at a long desk
MHJ 35: 在街北紧贴城墙的第一家…有的研究者认为这是税务所…"引子"…若没有这个"引子"，交税时税率就特别重…货主…手指货物与他说话…连城楼上值班的人也探出头来张望
YH21: 按理说城门内的第一个建筑应该是城防机关…进城的第一家却是场务，也就是税务所

landmarks.name: 軍巡鋪屋
landmarks.line: 本是防火的鋪屋，如今堆滿酒桶。
landmarks.line_en: Once a fire-watch post, now stacked with wine casks.
landmarks.src: 余辉 2023: the fire post now holds the troops' wine casks; 《东京梦华录》卷三 防火 '每坊巷三百步许，有军巡铺屋一所'
landmarks.long: 孫羊正店東邊一間臨街的屋子，地上排著打了鐵箍的大木桶，正是《東京夢華錄》說的「梢桶」，正店用它裝酒。桶上擱著水桶，一根滅火的麻搭橫在上面。余輝認出這本是防火的軍巡鋪屋，該存水的地方卻放滿了酒桶；屋裏的弓手有的拉弓試弦，有的綁護腕、繫護腰，準備押運禁軍的酒。故宮只說屋裏的人像在準備出發，韓森則以為這是賣弓箭的鋪子。這裏從余輝之說。
landmarks.long_en: East of Sun Yang's Main Tavern is a street-front room where big wooden barrels with iron hoops stand in rows on the ground: the very “shaotong” casks that Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital describes, which main taverns use to carry wine. Buckets sit on top of the casks, and a fire-swab for putting out fires lies across them. Yu Hui recognises this as a patrol post for fire watch, where water should be stored but wine casks are piled instead; the archers inside are pulling bows to test the strings, or tying on wrist guards and waist guards, getting ready to escort the wine of the Imperial Guard. The Palace Museum says only that the people inside seem to be preparing to set out, and Hansen thinks it is a shop selling bows and arrows. Here we follow Yu Hui.
landmarks.quote: 每坊巷三百步許，有軍巡鋪屋一所。
landmarks.quote_en: Every three hundred paces along the wards and lanes there is one patrol post.
landmarks.cite: 余輝〈十大看點〉〈最後三問〉・《東京夢華錄》・故宮名畫記・韓森
landmarks.cite_en: Yu Hui, Ten Highlights and The Last Three Questions · Dreams of Splendour of the Eastern Capital · Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Hansen
longSrc: map S5.bld.wine_depot, S5.prop.casks_5665, casks_west_5525 (hooped casks, buckets on top, the 麻搭 across)
DJ 卷三 般载杂卖: 酒正店多以此载酒梢桶矣。梢桶如长水桶
YH21: 军巡铺…这些桶本来储存的是消防用水…变成了军酒转运站…麻搭
YH15 看点九: 拉满弓试弦…系护腰…缠护腕; 奉命前来"正店"武力押送军酒
MHJ 37: 仿佛是在进行出发前的准备工作

landmarks.name: 城樓
landmarks.line: 樓內架著一面大鼓，暮時擊鼓。
landmarks.line_en: A great drum hangs inside, beaten at dusk.
landmarks.src: 名画记 33 雄伟的城楼 '楼内明显可见一个鼓架，上面装置了一个大鼓'; 余辉 2014 城上暮鼓
landmarks.long: 這是全卷最大的建築：廡殿頂，重重斗拱把屋簷挑得老遠，故宮說它有「大鵬展翅」的氣勢。樓內看得見一副鼓架，架著一面大鼓，余輝為這一景取名「城上暮鼓」。門額上只寫一個「門」字，城名用幾點帶過，余輝以為畫家有意不點明。樓門口獨立一人，余輝說是更夫，正低頭看稅務所前的爭吵；韓森卻說他是遊人，因為他望著城裏，不像守衛那樣望著城外。
landmarks.long_en: This is the largest building in the whole scroll: a hip roof, with layer upon layer of brackets pushing the eaves far out, which the Palace Museum says has the bearing of a “great roc spreading its wings.” Inside, a drum stand with a great drum can be seen, and Yu Hui names this scene “Evening Drum on the City Wall.” The plaque bears only the single character “Gate,” and the name of the city is skipped over with a few dots; Yu Hui thinks the painter meant not to say. A lone figure stands at the tower door, whom Yu Hui calls the night watchman, looking down at the quarrel in front of the Tax Office; Hansen says he is a sightseer, because he looks toward the city rather than out toward the country as a guard would.
landmarks.cite: 故宮名畫記・余輝・韓森
landmarks.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Yu Hui · Hansen
longSrc: MHJ 33: 最大的建筑物…庑殿顶，多重硕大的斗拱将屋檐外挑，使整个屋顶有大鹏展翅的动感…楼内明显可见一个鼓架，上面装置了一个大鼓
SEC §1.2: YH14 城上暮鼓

YH15 看点八: 惊动了城楼上的更夫向下张望
SEC §3: Hansen: "a tourist, he gazes at the people inside the wall, not outside, where a guard would look"

landmarks.name: 平橋
landmarks.line_en: At the railings, people watch spring water and fish.
landmarks.src: 余辉《深度游》第五段 平桥城门; 邵琦: watchers at the railings; 余辉 2015 桥头观水
landmarks.long: 護城河上一座平平的木橋，兩側有木欄，欄邊擠滿了看水的人，有的倚欄看春水游魚，有的背過身來閒談。兩個小乞兒伸著手向遊人討錢，故宮名畫記寫得仔細：有人裝作沒聽見，有人怕掃了雅興，給一文錢打發他們走。戴頭巾的讀書人和穿短衣的苦力在同一道橋欄邊並肩，韓森說這座橋是各色人等的一幅群像。
landmarks.long_en: A flat wooden bridge crosses the moat, with wooden rails on both sides, and the rails are crowded with people looking at the water; some lean over to watch the spring water and the fish, others turn their backs and chat. Two little beggar boys hold out their hands to passers-by, and the Palace Museum's notes describe it closely: some pretend not to hear, some, afraid of spoiling the pleasant mood, give a coin to send them off. A scholar in a headscarf and a labourer in a short jacket stand shoulder to shoulder at the same railing, and Hansen says this bridge is a group portrait of all kinds of people.
landmarks.cite: 故宮名畫記・邵琦・韓森・畫中所見
landmarks.cite_en: Palace Museum, Minghuaji · Shao Qi · Hansen · What the painting shows
longSrc: map S5.str.moat_bridge: flat timber bridge, plank railings, sightseers lean on both railings
SEC §3: 邵琦 有不少人在桥栏杆边观鱼; YH15 看点三: 清明节人们喜欢到河上观赏春水和游鱼
MHJ 32: 两个乞儿…其中两个人任凭…只装作没听见。另外两个也许怕乞儿破坏他们看风景的雅兴，伸出手给了他一文钱
SEC §3: Literati in kerchiefs and labourers…; Hansen "a tableau of different social groups"
